question.text: The Democratic Unionist Party has long been the majority party in Northern Ireland's parliament, which convenes at Stormont Castle in this capital city.
question.clue: In the 1970s, a terrorist group based on this city's Shankill Road slit the throats of numerous Catholic residents and their leader was later gunned down by the Provisional IRA.

swap.leadin: Taoiseach [pr. TEA-SHICH] Brian Cowen, the prime minister of this nation, was incriminated in 2009 after revelations that this country's central bank had hidden millions of euros worth of loans.
swap.text: Name this country which was partitioned in two in 1920, then declared a "Free State" two years later.
swap.clue: Its war for independence is known as the Black and Tan War, and the Battle of the Boyne was fought in this nation.

question.text: This Irish political figure avoided being executed following the Easter Rising, and opposed the Anglo-Irish Treaty; he would later serve as President of Ireland until his death in 1975.
question.clue: This leader's American citizenship allowed him to escape execution after the Easter Rising.

swap.leadin: Eoin ("owen") MacNeill gave orders to halt mobilization in this event, but Patrick Pearse (peers) and Tom Clarke continued anyway.
swap.text: Name this rebellion, which began with a raid on the General Post Office. Roger Casement asked for German aid for this event and was later executed for his participation.
swap.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter uprising or Easter Rebellion or Éirí Amach na Cásca or Éirí Amach 1916 or Aiséirí na Cásca; prompt on Easter or Easter 1916 or the Rising]
swap.clue: Tom Clarke planned this event, and, like Joseph Plunkett and John MacBride, he was executed for taking part.

question.text: This paramilitary organization tried to assassinate Thatcher in the Brighton Hotel bombing. During her term, a member of this group, Bobby Sands, died from a hunger strike in Maze Prison.
question.clue: This group placed a bomb inside a fishing boat that killed the last Viceroy of India, Lord Mountbatten, and a member of this organization named Bobby Sands became a martyr after dying during a hunger strike.

swap.text: The Dail Eireann sits in this city, the capital of Ireland.
swap.clue: Patrick Pearse proclaimed a republic in this city during a 1916 rebellion.

question.leadin: This movement provides its name to four bills, the third of which was passed in 1914 but never implemented due to World War I.
question.text: Name this movement calling for the self-governance of a former country of the United Kingdom.
question.answerHtml: Irish Home Rule [prompt on just “Home Rule”; prompt on “Irish Independence,” “Irish autonomy,” or other similar answers]
question.clue: Anti-Papist fears were cited by opponents of this cause, such as the Orange League.

swap.leadin: Name some key figures in the movement for, and early period of, Irish Home Rule.
swap.text: This 19th century leader and founder of the Irish Parliamentary Party spent most of his career advocating for Home Rule, and served as a member of the House of Commons for decades.
swap.clue: The reputation of this man was tarnished by a letter forged by Richard Pigott, which appeared to condone the murders of Thomas Burke and Lord Cavendish in Phoenix Park.

question.text: The Croke Park massacre of soccer fans was among the worst offenses of this notoriously brutal unit of British irregulars, who were brought to Ireland in 1920 to root out independence leaders and were nicknamed for their patchwork uniforms.
question.clue: The first man they formally executed was Kevin Barry, whom they captured on the same day as their sack of Balbriggan.

swap.text: This leader of the Land League gave the speech that incited the original boycott. As an MP, he convinced members of the Liberal Party to support Irish Home Rule.
swap.clue: From jail, this man negotiated an agreement with William Gladstone that included concessions for land tenants called the Kilmainham Treaty.

question.text: This man served as spokesman for the rebellion, and he gave both the orders for it to begin and for the final surrender. He was executed by firing squad like co-leader James Connolly.
question.clue: This man praised war for warming the "heart of the earth" with the "red wine of battlefields," a metaphor reflecting his mystical belief in "blood sacrifice."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about poor British governmental responses to hunger strikes.
swap.text: Margaret Thatcher pronounced this IRA member to be a "criminal" who "chose to take his own life" after he died following a 66-day hunger strike in Maze Prison.
swap.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

question.leadin: Identify the following about David Ricardo's worst nightmare--the Corn Laws.
question.text: The Corn Laws began to be repealed with the onset of this event, which lasted from 1845 to around 1850 and had its effects worsened by the Gregory clause. Many then emigrated from the Emerald Isle to countries like the U.S.
question.clue: This situation was worsened by the system of absentee landlords as well as by the Corn Laws.

swap.leadin: About ninety followers of Hugh O'Neill and Rory O'Donnell fled this region for Spain in what was called the "Flight of the Earls."
swap.text: Name this northeastern region of Ireland, which was later heavily settled by Protestant Scots. Its traditional flag features a red hand.
swap.clue: This region was the center of the Flight of the Earls that escaped from Oriel and Tyrconnell which were both in this region.

question.text: This Provisional IRA member was elected to Parliament while imprisoned at HM Prison Maze. He died in May 1981 after leading a hunger strike in protest against the removal of the Special Category Status for IRA prisoners.
question.clue: During Thatcher's first term, this member of the IRA led a 1981 hunger strike against Ireland's "Special Category Status." He died of starvation in the Maze Prison.

swap.text: This Irishman published a namesake report detailing this horrors of the Belgian Congo. He was arrested and executed as a conspirator after the Easter Rising.
swap.clue: This man's lawyer, A. M. Sullivan, tried to argue that there was a comma after the word "realm" in the clause "realm or elsewhere" in the 1351 statute this man was charged with violating; as a result, this man was said to have been "hanged on a comma."

question.text: A small French army led by Jean Humbert proclaimed the Republic of Connacht after winning the Battle of Castlebar during this uprising, sometimes named for a secret society founded by Wolfe Tone.
question.answerHtml: Irish Rebellion of 1798 [or United Irishmen Rebellion; accept equivalents mentioning the year 1798; prompt on ‘98]
question.clue: The losing side of this conflict were defeated at the Battle of Vinegar (+) Hill, and France tacitly provided support for this revolt thanks to the efforts of Wolfe Tone, who died before his planned execution after this event.

swap.leadin: After Garrett Fitzgerald appeared on a television show on this station, Brian Lenihan claimed "of mature recollection" that he did not make a telephone call to the leader of the country.
swap.text: Name this television station that aired the political debate program Questions and Answers in the 1990s. "Gay" Byrne hosted The Late Late for 37 years on this Irish public service broadcaster.
swap.answerHtml: RTE [or Raidio Teilifis Eireann] (The show Byrne presented was The Late Late)

question.text: In 1889 Parnell was politically ruined when his affair with this longtime mistress was revealed. Her husband, an Irish MP, filed for divorce and named Parnell as corespondent.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Dark Age saint.
swap.text: Seventh century biographers Tirechan and Muirchu tell tales of his hostility to the Druids. More reliable is the humble rustic Latin of his own "Confession."
swap.clue: This Christian saint who, according to legend, taught the Trinity using a shamrock and exiled all snakes from the isle where he preached, Ireland.
